name: Zillow Group, Inc.

profile.description: Zillow Group operates the leading real estate marketplace in the United States, connecting buyers, sellers, renters, and agents through its digital platforms. The company operates across Residential (agent advertising and connections), Rentals (multifamily marketplace), Mortgages (purchase loan origination), and Other segments. Key properties include Zillow.com, Trulia, HotPads, and StreetEasy, collectively reaching approximately 220 million monthly unique users. CEO Jeremy Wacksman is executing a 'housing super app' strategy integrating search, touring, financing, and transaction management. Revenue of $2.69B TTM.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Zillow has evolved from a home valuation website into a multi-product 'housing super app' integrating search, agent connections, mortgage origination, and rentals — mortgage origination volume surged 96% and rentals revenue grew 42% YoY in Q1 2026, demonstrating successful business model expansion [1]. The failed iBuyer pivot (2021-2022) was a significant misstep but the recovery and strategic refocus represents genuine adaptability. AI Deployment (1/2): CEO Wacksman told WSJ that 'AI is reducing friction in real estate,' with AI embedded across search personalization, predictive intelligence, and agent productivity tools [2]. Employees have been retrained to incorporate AI into their workflows, and new leadership (CPO Christopher Roberts) was appointed to drive AI-focused product work. However, no specific AI-driven revenue or cost savings have been quantified. Market Share (2/2): Zillow is the undisputed category leader in online real estate with ~220M monthly unique users, dominant brand awareness, and no close second in consumer real estate search — the Zillow Zestimate has become a household term [2]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Enhanced Zillow Listing Agent, AI-powered touring experiences, and mortgage expansion are in progress, but specific launch dates and revenue visibility are limited; management guided for mid-teens total revenue growth and ~30% rentals growth for full-year 2026 [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): As a technology-first real estate platform, Zillow's R&D spending is above real estate industry peers, with continuous investment in AI, machine learning, and platform engineering.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Zillow's mission to 'give people the power to unlock life's next chapter' is specific, service-oriented, and distinctive — it identifies the audience (homebuyers, sellers, renters), the purpose (empowerment in life transitions), and connects to something bigger than transactions [2]. The mission has guided product decisions including expansion into mortgages, rentals, and AI-powered search, and survived the iBuyer crisis. However, it hasn't been tested through decades of consistent execution or leadership transitions. Community Impact (1/2): Zillow committed $1M+ to social and housing justice nonprofits, pursued pay equity ($1.01 per $1 for women in comparable roles as of 2018), and set Scope 1 and 2 emissions reduction targets of 46% by 2030 from a 2019 base year [3]. These are meaningful but not transformative community investments. Employee Retention (0/2): 7,068 employees with 3.09% headcount growth in 2025, but the 2022 layoff of 25% of the workforce after the iBuyer shutdown creates a mixed retention picture — no specific tenure or turnover data is available. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying identified in available data.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Zillow's financial profile is improving but still transitioning — Q1 2026 revenue grew 18.4% YoY to $708M with net income of $46M (6% margin, up 520bps YoY), demonstrating the emerging profitability inflection [1]. Forward P/E of approximately 14x and forward PEG of 0.33 reflect attractive growth-adjusted valuation after the stock's 52.9% YTD decline to $31.15 [4][5]. Debt-to-equity of 9% is excellent, and the company operates with minimal leverage. However, trailing profit margin of only 2.27% and ROE of 0.47% reflect that Zillow is still in the early stages of translating revenue growth into meaningful profitability [4]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of -5.0% is severely distorted by the iBuyer revenue cycle (massive revenue in 2021-2022, then collapse) and understates the organic growth trajectory of the core marketplace business.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Zillow's core business is protected by powerful network effects — 220M monthly users and relationships with hundreds of thousands of real estate agents create a marketplace flywheel that AI cannot easily replicate [2]. Real estate transactions inherently involve physical-world activities (home tours, inspections, closings) and heavily regulated processes (mortgage origination, title insurance) that AI cannot substitute. However, AI assistants and agents could theoretically disintermediate Zillow's search-to-agent connection model by directly matching buyers with agents or properties, bypassing the platform entirely. AI-powered property valuation tools could erode the Zestimate's competitive advantage. The company faces moderate but manageable AI exposure — the physical and regulatory nature of real estate provides meaningful protection. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI is embedded throughout Zillow's platform — search personalization, predictive intelligence, agent productivity tools, and the new CPO appointment focused on AI-driven product development demonstrate that AI is actively enhancing the user experience and driving engagement [2].

infinite_game.summary: Zillow demonstrates genuine infinite game characteristics in its Just Cause and competitive mindset, but the iBuyer debacle and subsequent 25% workforce layoff in 2022 revealed the limits of the company's commitment when faced with real financial pressure. Under CEO Wacksman (since 2024), Zillow is rebuilding toward a housing super app vision with AI at the center, showing strategic ambition and recovery capability that Sinek would view as promising but unproven.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Give people the power to unlock life's next chapter' is a genuine and distinctive cause — it's specific to Zillow, service-oriented, idealistic (home-buying as a life transition, not just a transaction), and inclusive [2]. The purpose has guided product expansion into mortgages, rentals, and AI-powered search. It survived the iBuyer crisis: rather than abandoning the mission, Zillow refocused on making the existing marketplace better. However, the cause has not been tested through decades of execution or a leadership transition — Wacksman only became CEO in 2024.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Recent leadership promotions (CPO Christopher Roberts, SVP Marissa Brooks, SVP Jon Lim) suggest investment in developing talent from within rather than hiring externally, and the 7,068-person workforce grew 3.09% in 2025 after the 2022 contraction [2]. However, the 2022 layoff of 25% of the workforce after the iBuyer shutdown was a severe trust breach — employees who joined for the iBuyer vision were abruptly let go. The cultural recovery under Wacksman appears genuine but remains incomplete.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Zillow's competitive language consistently focuses on building better products and reducing friction rather than defeating specific competitors like Redfin, Realtor.com, or Homes.com [2]. CEO Wacksman frames competition as 'opportunities' for improvement and discusses AI's potential to help the entire industry, not just Zillow. The company's response to the iBuyer failure — learning from it and pivoting to a better strategy — exemplifies using competitive setbacks for self-improvement rather than blame.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The iBuyer pivot was a bold, transformative bet that ultimately failed — Zillow committed billions to buying and reselling homes, fundamentally departing from its marketplace model [2]. While the failure cost $881M in write-downs and 2,000+ jobs, the willingness to attempt a complete business model transformation demonstrates genuine existential flexibility. The recovery and refocus on the 'housing super app' strategy shows adaptability. However, the pivot was driven partly by competitive fear (OpenDoor, Offerpad) rather than purely by the Just Cause.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Zillow's willingness to exit the iBuyer business at a $881M loss — publicly admitting failure rather than doubling down — required significant corporate courage [2]. The subsequent investment in mortgage origination (96% volume growth), rentals marketplace (42% revenue growth), and AI integration demonstrates reinvestment in long-term capabilities [1]. However, the iBuyer exit was also forced by the scale of losses, making it partially a survival decision rather than a purely courageous choice.

investment_thesis: Zillow is the undisputed leader in online real estate with 220M monthly users and no close second, now executing a 'housing super app' strategy that is driving accelerating revenue diversification — Q1 2026 revenue grew 18.4% to $708M, with mortgage origination volume up 96% and rentals revenue up 42% to $183M (multifamily up 57%) [1]. The stock's 52.9% YTD decline to $31.15 has created a compelling valuation: forward P/E of approximately 14x and forward PEG of 0.33 for a company guiding mid-teens revenue growth with meaningful back-half margin expansion [1][4]. Net income margin improved 520bps YoY to 6% in Q1, and adjusted EBITDA of $182M (26% margin) demonstrates the operating leverage emerging as the marketplace model scales. Zillow's AI-powered platform strategy under CEO Wacksman is differentiated and gaining traction.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on Zillow's dependence on the US housing market, which remains structurally challenged by elevated mortgage rates and affordability constraints — existing home sales remain well below the 5-6M annual pace that prevailed pre-pandemic [1]. The 52.9% YTD stock decline reflects investor concerns that macro headwinds could persist through 2026-2027, limiting transaction volume growth regardless of Zillow's platform improvements. Trailing profit margin of just 2.27% and ROE of 0.47% demonstrate that Zillow has not yet proven it can convert revenue growth into meaningful shareholder returns [4]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of -5.0% — distorted by the iBuyer cycle — raises questions about the stability of Zillow's revenue model. The company's dual-class share structure (Z/ZG) concentrates control with co-founders Rich Barton and Lloyd Frink, limiting shareholder influence. Competitive threats from CoStar/Homes.com (investing $1B+ in agent advertising) could pressure Zillow's core Residential revenue segment.
key_catalysts: Mortgage origination volume up 96% YoY in Q1 2026 — as Zillow captures a larger share of purchase mortgage flow from its 220M-user marketplace, this high-margin revenue stream could drive significant margin expansion [1]

Rentals revenue growing 42% YoY ($183M in Q1, multifamily up 57%) with management guiding approximately 30% full-year growth — the rentals marketplace is becoming a second major growth engine beyond residential [1]

Forward PEG of 0.33 at $31.15 represents extreme growth-adjusted undervaluation — any housing market recovery or continued margin expansion could trigger substantial multiple re-rating from current depressed levels [4][5]
key_risks: US housing market remains structurally challenged by elevated mortgage rates and affordability constraints — existing home sales volume well below pre-pandemic norms limits Zillow's transaction-based revenue potential [1]

52.9% YTD stock decline reflects deep investor skepticism about near-term earnings power — trailing profit margin of 2.27% and ROE of 0.47% demonstrate Zillow has not yet proven sustainable profitability [4]

CoStar Group/Homes.com investing $1B+ to compete directly with Zillow's agent advertising business, creating a well-funded competitive threat to the core Residential revenue segment that represents 64% of total revenue [1]
